requirements.title: ACHAR arguments have integer I and optional scalar integer constant KIND
requirements.definition: The I argument to ACHAR shall be of type integer, and the optional KIND argument shall be a scalar integer constant expression.

pending.achar-i-argument-integer: Future positive controls call ACHAR with integer I values; noninteger I source shapes remain source-control only with no local diagnostic claim.
pending.achar-kind-argument-scalar-integer-const: Future positive controls use an integer constant KIND such as KIND('a') or selected_char_kind result where available; nonconstant or nonscalar KIND shapes are not local diagnostic facets.

requirements.title: ACHAR result has length one and selected character kind
requirements.definition: ACHAR returns a character result of length one; if KIND is present the result kind is the specified kind value, otherwise it is default character kind.

pending.achar-result-length-one: Future fixture initializes a nondefault integer code such as 88 and asserts LEN(ACHAR(88)) == 1.
pending.achar-result-kind-from-kind-argument: Future guarded fixture chooses a supported character kind, calls ACHAR with KIND=that constant, and asserts KIND(result) equals the specified value.
pending.achar-result-default-character-kind-when: Future fixture asserts KIND(ACHAR(88)) equals KIND('X') when KIND is omitted.

requirements.title: ACHAR maps representable ASCII code values to ASCII collating positions
requirements.source: 16.9.3 p5 first sentence representable case; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF377.
requirements.definition: If I is in the range 0 through 127 and the processor can represent that character in the result character kind, ACHAR(I) is the character in position I of the ASCII collating sequence.

pending.achar-ascii-code-88-is-x: Future exact fixture asserts ACHAR(88) has LEN 1 and value 'X', using the source example only as illustration of the p5 mapping.
pending.achar-ascii-digit-and-letter-codes: Future exact fixture checks a small table of representable default characters such as ACHAR(48) == '0', ACHAR(65) == 'A', and ACHAR(122) == 'z', with LEN checks before equality.

requirements.title: ACHAR results are processor dependent outside representable ASCII mapping
requirements.source: 16.9.3 p5 otherwise clause; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF377.
requirements.definition: When I is outside the representable ASCII mapping case, the ACHAR result is processor dependent.

pending.achar-outside-representable-range-proces: No portable oracle may require a particular character for an out-of-range code or for an unrepresentable result kind. Future tests must avoid exact expectations in this domain.

requirements.title: ACHAR and IACHAR round-trip default representable characters
requirements.source: 16.9.3 p5 final sentence; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF377.
requirements.definition: ACHAR(IACHAR(C)) shall have the value C for any character C capable of representation as a default character.
